summary: Ajit Ranjan Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. A former pupil of Vidhusekhara Bhattacharya, he served as an Ex-Puranchand Nahar Fellow at the University of Calcutta.
Akane Saito is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied under Alexis Sanderson and held a post at the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Akifumi Naito (b. 1956) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University, Honganji-ha Shogakuin, and under Gadjin Nagao (1979–2002), holding posts at Ryukoku University, the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism, Kyoto Women's University, and Gyoshin Buddhist Academy.

Akihiko Akamatsu (b. 1953) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Kyoto University (~1976–1978), the University of Paris, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University (~1978–1983), later serving as Associate Professor at Kyushu University (~1989–2000) and Professor at Kyoto University (~2000–2019).

Akihiro Oda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under doctoral supervisor Kazuo Hyodo and committee members Robert F. Rhodes, Fumio Ouchi, and Yoshihide Yoshizu. In 2013, he served as Professor of Buddhist Studies at Otani University.

Akiko Walley is a scholar of Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1997–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), later holding a post at the University of Oregon (2009–2016).

Akimichi Eda works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. at the University of Marburg (~2000–2005) under Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki, Khangkar Tsultrim Kelsang, Muneo Tokunaga, and Werner Knobl.
Akio Donohashi (b. 1948) works in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1978) and served as a Professor at Kobe University (1990–1991).

Akio Minoura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed graduate studies at Otani University under Yoshifumi Honjo, held an overseas research post at Stanford University (2012–2013), and served as an Associate Professor at Otani University.

Akio Tanabe (b. 1964) specializes in Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–1993) and held posts as an Associate Professor at Kyoto University (~2001–2010) and at the University of Tokyo (~2016).
Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1932–1937) and served there as a group leader (~1966–1975).
Akira Hataya (b. 1949) is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College and as Professor Emeritus at Otani University (~2015).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Shoson Miyamoto and at the University of Tokyo (~1938–1959), where he was a professor (1954–1978). He also held posts at Waseda, Rissho, Komazawa, and ICPBS.

Akira Miyaji (b. 1945) specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Nagoya University (~1964–1991) and held posts at Kyoto University, Hirosaki University, Nagoya University (Emeritus Professor ~2006), Ryukoku University, and the Ryukoku Museum.

Akira Mukai (b. 1942) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral coursework at Hokkaido University (~-1977), where he served as an assistant (~1977–1982), and later became a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College.

Akira Omine (1929–2018) was a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1949–1957), he held posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University (Professor Emeritus ~1993), Ryukoku University, and the Research Institute of Shin Buddhism.

Akira Onda (1925–2015) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1947–1951). He served as a professor at Toyo University (~1968–1986) and held posts at Kawamura Gakuen Women's University and the University of Tokyo.

Akira Sadakata (b. 1936) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1955–1959) and the University of Paris (1963–1965), under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, and served as Associate Professor at Tokai University (~1970–2007).

Akira Saito (b. 1950) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied under Jikido Takasaki at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD at ANU, later holding posts at Mie University, the University of Tokyo, and ICPBS.

Akira Shimada works in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan, and under Daud Ali and Ulrich Pagel, holding posts at the British Museum and SUNY New Paltz.
